verdict.rationale: MotherDuck Flights let users run Python jobs on a schedule for ingest, transformation, and operational tasks. The jobs can be built by an agent and deployed in MotherDuck, with the platform handling the runtime, scheduling, secrets, logging, and versioning. That covers the core of autonomous background automation. The evidence comes only from short product-page and getting-started blurbs. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of Flights (triggers beyond schedules, failure handling/alerting, run monitoring), and independent or hands-on corroboration that scheduled jobs run reliably.
